purpose: Reviewable language semantics and SNN execution expectations for joint development.

execution_evidence.scope: 22 direct scalar/module checks plus native process, frontend-only and C++ compatibility evidence; not a run of all 25 catalog cases.
partial_coverage_notes: Identity uses distinct canonical local module paths, not resolved versioned package origins.
Scope/capture fixtures exercise equivalent scalar cases, not every exact trace or unwind form in the catalog.
Function, binding and type diagnostics cover named examples, not all variants in CS-08/CS-11/CS-13.
The frame fixture preserves A by program construction/assertions, not a checked immutable-view type.
Scan-before-execution is checked by rejecting a broken dependency before an earlier print can execute; the distinct scan/encounter order scenario CS-18 is not executed.
No regional-pointer, escaping-capture, concurrency or package-version acceptance.

cases.setup: Export @s; import it as @a and @b from the same declaration.
Two coexisting package origins each declare the same textual symbol name.

cases.note: Structured early-return/unwind paths require the same restoration; exact failure syntax is not selected.

cases.topic: capture by value and invocation mode
cases.setup: Evaluate effect @x = 1, then define procedure @p whose body reads @x.
steps: Evaluate effect @x = 2 in the caller scope.

cases.setup: @p captures @x = 1; its body evaluates effect @x = @x + 1, then reads @x. Caller @x is 7.
cases.derivation: Each perform installs the original capture; behave starts with the current caller binding. Both modes restore the body-local effect on return; no write-through assignment exists.

cases.setup: @p refers to a definition-site lexical constant 4 and effect @x captured at 1; caller has an unrelated same-spelling lexical constant 9 and @x = 7.
steps: perform @p and observe the lexical constant and @x.
behave @p and observe the lexical constant and @x.

cases.setup: @q reads @gain and was defined at @gain = 5. @p executes behave @q and is defined with the source @q binding and @gain = 2. Caller retains that @q and has @gain = 9.
cases.note: A required-symbol analysis must account for q through behave; it cannot inspect only direct names in p.

reject_in_function: Call a helper that executes such effects.
cases.note: Diagnostic spelling and the internal effect-summary representation are proposed implementation work.

reject: Native heap pointer as a third capture kind.
Stack pointer captured as an escaping reference.
Implicit heap boxing of a user closure to extend its lifetime.
Copy/move of a regional object as a capture.
cases.note: Cross-region references remain a placeholder under H-101; no encoding or exception to the two capture forms is selected.

cases.setup: Two threads explicitly establish different values of the same imported symbol, 3 and 8.
cases.note: This does not choose thread creation inheritance or task/fiber semantics.

cases: One symbol used as incompatible value types.
A write through an immutable frame-A view.
A frame/region reference retained past its valid lifetime.
cases.expected: A specified static diagnostic or explicit checked boundary; exact rules remain to be qualified.
cases.note: Required-binding absence is separately specified as a compile-time error in CS-13; these representation/type details remain proposals.
Hand-derived exact-integer data-flow fixture, not an adopted neuron equation, simulation or training result. Source reads must also leave A unchanged.

cases.setup: Compile a demanded entry with its module initialization and caller paths; do not compile modules independently.

cases.path: behave @p reaches a read of @x with an active binding.
behave @p reaches a read of @x with no supplying scope.
perform @p requires a captured @x that its definition path could not supply.
cases.expected: Compilation error; no fallback to caller @x.

cases.path: One reachable branch supplies @x and another reaches its required use without it.
cases.expected: Compilation error on the uncovered path.

cases.note: Algorithm, diagnostics and recursion summarization remain implementation design; no runtime unbound-value policy is selected.

cases: A procedure definition uses a symbol and belongs to dynamic scope.
A bare-name procedure definition is not a second allowed procedure mechanism.
Module top-level dynamic scope is its initialization procedure.
cases.note: Module execution scope closes after top-level execution; only using/import bring effective resources into the receiver. Scanning itself does not execute initialization; repeated/cyclic encounters remain open.

cases: Write a symbol only with effect @name = rhs.
Reject plain or compound assignment as an alternate symbolic write.
Compose evaluation as expressions, using void for explicitly no meaningful returned value.
effect @x = 3 evaluates to 3, the newly bound value.
open_details: Scope-result selection and compound-expression evaluation order.

cases.setup: A shared vocabulary declares @x with comments. A source procedure body uses an unqualified lexical helper and @x. Source helper result is 4 and definition capture is 1; receiving helper result is 9 and import definition capture is 7. Later caller @x is 8.
cases.note: using retains the source definition; import redefines its body in receiving scopes. A symbol alias alone does not create a fresh symbol or recapture a procedure. Binding/declaration syntax is not selected.

cases.topic: complete declaration scan without procedure execution
cases.setup: An entry depends on A and B, each with symbols/functions/literal bits globals and a registered procedure body.
expected: All dependency modules are scanned/loaded before entry execution semantics are compiled.
Scanning procedure @p records the definition/body without invoking it, installing its dynamic binding or capturing values.

cases.topic: dependency execution incorporation follows encounter order
cases.setup: Scan/load A, B and C; subsequent entry execution compilation encounters B then A, each once, and does not encounter C.
cases.expected: Scan order does not establish execution order; C scanning alone contributes no top-level execution semantics.
cases.limits: No repeated/cyclic encounters or branch-ordering policy is assumed. Every kind of cross-module reference is an encounter trigger under H-109.

cases.topic: registered body versus dynamic definition event
cases.setup: Register a procedure body that uses @x during scanning; its demanded definition/call paths are compiled later.
expected: Scanning does not snapshot a scanner-side @x value.
Capture refers to the definition event in the resulting execution semantics.
A required value missing on the applicable compiled path is a compilation error, despite successful declaration registration.

allowed_ordinary_definitions: bits global variable initialized by a bits literal or function call
cases.procedure_rule: A top-level procedure @name body is registered during scanning without execution semantics.
cases.excluded: Arbitrary top-level effect evaluation is not enabled during scanning.
open_details: Literal grammar, mutability/sharing and physical realization of bits globals.
Repeated/cyclic encounters and global realization; source module scope ends after its top-level execution.

cases.topic: top-level effects and procedure calls execute with the module
cases.setup: A module contains effect @x = value and perform/behave expressions targeting registered procedure definitions.
expected: The forms are allowed at module top level.
The scan retains expressions without installing @x, invoking procedures or capturing values.
Their behavior belongs to module execution in the resulting program; ordinary scoped binding and call-mode rules apply.

allowed: Function call producing the required bits value.
cases.not_authorized_as_a_function_initializer: A perform/behave procedure invocation; those are separately permitted top-level execution expressions.
expected: Scan records a function-call initializer without evaluating it.
Initializer evaluation belongs to module execution and the called function retains its pure input/output contract.
cases.limits: Global mutability, sharing, physical storage and final declaration syntax remain open.

cases.topic: every cross-module reference triggers execution semantics
cases.expected: Each kind triggers source-module execution-semantics incorporation during entry-driven compilation; scan-time loading alone does not execute it.
cases.limits: Repeated encounters and cycles are not fixed by this case.

cases.topic: source scope closes while using retains selected captures
cases.setup: Caller has @x = 7. Source top-level scope binds @x = 1 and defines @p reading it; using brings @p into the receiver.
cases.note: Only selected effective resources transfer through using/import. Source scoped bindings are restored; retained captures are values, not dangling stack references.
The result does not extend the binding lifetime beyond the enclosing scope.

limits: The complete catalog remains a specification; selected actual native prototype evidence is linked separately.
Candidate type/lifetime, initialization-composition and expression-result rules remain separate from confirmed user semantics. Missing required bindings are compilation errors.
No package-identity byte format, TLS ABI, cross-region pointer representation or neural model is selected.
